title: Multi-rank NCCL wait versus transfer
summary: See why one rank's NCCL interval can include peer wait as well as data movement.

verification.label: Measured multi-rank TorchTitan/PyTorch native CP
verification.implementation: TorchTitan Qwen3 model with PyTorch 2.9 native context_parallel, FlashAttention, CP=4, all-gather K/V rotation
verification.workload: Two dense Qwen-shaped layers, hidden 4096, 64 query heads, 4 KV heads, global sequence 16384, BF16
verification.measurement: Ranks 0 and 3 from one Nsight Systems capture; common GPU timestamp origin
verification.timeline: Exact stream-7 kernels, dependency wait intervals, and stream-23 NCCL all-gather intervals for ranks 0 and 3

description: Ranks 0 and 3 move the same K/V payload and finish the same collective at almost the same time. Rank 3's NCCL kernel starts about 0.75 ms earlier, so its longer bar cannot represent extra bytes.
The rank 3 interval includes time resident while peer kernels have not yet started making collective progress, followed by transfer and overlap. A single-rank trace cannot separate those components.
insight: A long NCCL bar is not a direct bandwidth measurement: it may contain peer wait, transfer, and compute contention.
hint: Compare the same collective across ranks. If one bar starts earlier but they finish together, the extra width is not extra payload transfer.
explanation: the aligned ranks show why NCCL kernel duration must not be interpreted as pure send time.

Rank 3 layer 0 forward K/V all-gather GPU kernel
blocks.description: Same payload as rank 0. Its earlier GPU start makes this interval include waiting for peer progress as well as transfer and compute contention.
